passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes included in Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K. This Item generally discusses 2026 and 2025 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2026 and 2025. Discussions of 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024 are not included, and can be found in “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Part II, Item 7 of the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 27, 2025. Product, Service and Software Announcements The Company announces new product, service and software offerings at various times during the year. Significant announcements during fiscal year 2026 included the following: First Quarter 2026: • 14-inch MacBook Pro • iPad Pro • Apple Vision Pro Second Quarter 2026: • iPad Air • iPhone 17e • MacBook Neo, MacBook Air and MacBook Pro • AirPods Max 2 Third Quarter 2026: • iOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, iPadOS 27, watchOS 27, visionOS 27 and tvOS 27 • Siri AI Fourth Quarter 2026: • Mac mini and Mac Studio • iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone 18 Pro • Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 • AirPods 5 Macroeconomic Conditions Macroeconomic conditions, including inflation, interest rates, component pricing, supply constraints and currency fluctuations, have directly and indirectly impacted, and could in the future materially impact, the Company’s business, revenue, costs, gross margin, results of operations and financial condition. The Company is experiencing supply constraints and rising costs driven by industry-wide supply-demand imbalances for key components, including advanced semiconductors, memory and storage. The Company expects these trends to intensify for memory and storage components. Actions, such as price increases, that have been and may in the future be taken by the Company may not effectively mitigate these negative impacts, and may also reduce demand for the Company’s products. Apple Inc. | 2026 Form 10-K | 24 Tariffs and Other Measures Beginning in the second quarter of 2025, new tariffs were announced on imports to the U.S., including additional tariffs on imports from China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the EU, among others. In response, several countries have imposed, or threatened to impose, reciprocal tariffs on imports from the U.S. and other retaliatory measures. On January 14, 2026, initial results were published of the previously announced U.S. Department of Commerce investigation under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, as amended, into imports of semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and their derivative products, including downstream products that contain semiconductors. The announcement of the initial results of the investigation did not impose any additional tariffs affecting the Company’s products. Separately, on February 20, 2026, the Supreme Court issued a ruling striking down certain tariffs previously imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act of 1977. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The following summarizes factors that could have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, reputation, results of operations, financial condition and stock price. The Company may not be able to accurately predict, control or mitigate these risks. Statements in this section are based on the Company’s beliefs and opinions regarding matters that could materially adversely affect the Company in the future and are not representations as to whether such matters have or have not occurred previously. The risks and uncertainties described below are not exhaustive and should not be considered a complete statement of all potential risks or uncertainties that the Company faces or may face in the future. This section should be read in conjunction with Part II, Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes in Part II, Item 8, “Financial Statements and Supplementary Data” of this Form 10-K. Apple Inc. | 2026 Form 10-K | 5 Macroeconomic and Industry Risks The Company’s operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions. The Company has international operations with sales outside the U.S. representing a majority of the Company’s total net sales. In addition, the Company’s global supply chain is large and complex and a majority of the Company’s supplier facilities, including manufacturing and assembly sites, are located outside the U.S. Adverse macroeconomic conditions, including slow growth or recession, high unemployment, inflation, tighter credit, higher interest rates, and currency fluctuations, can adversely impact consumer confidence and spending and materially adversely affect demand for the Company’s products and services. In addition, consumer confidence and spending can be materially adversely affected by changes in fiscal and monetary policy, financial market volatility, declines in income or asset values, and other economic factors. Uncertainty about, or a decline in, global or regional economic conditions can also have a significant impact on the Company’s developers, suppliers, contract manufacturers, logistics providers, distributors, cellular network carriers and other channel partners. Potential outcomes include financial instability, inability to obtain credit, and insolvency. Adverse economic conditions can also lead to increased credit and collectibility risk on the Company’s trade receivables; the failure of derivative counterparties and other financial institutions; limitations on the Company’s ability to issue new debt; reduced liquidity; and declines in the fair values of the Company’s financial instruments. These and other impacts can materially adversely affect the Company’s business, results of operations, financial condition and stock price. The Company’s business can be impacted by political events, trade and other international disputes, geopolitical tensions, conflict, terrorism, natural disasters, public health issues, industrial accidents and other business interruptions. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin expanded year over year and sits well above the sector median, reflecting pricing power in hardware and a growing services mix; this earnings quality underpins cash generation through the supply-driven cost pressure flagged in the MD&A.

Gross leverage fell versus the prior year and remains far below the sector median, while net leverage on a cash-and-investments basis sits deep inside the lowest risk band with substantial headroom to the next threshold.

key_risks.text: The risk factors highlight dependence on a large offshore supply chain and non-US sales, with adverse macro conditions, tariffs and trade disputes able to hit demand, component costs and receivables; the MD&A confirms memory and storage cost inflation is expected to intensify.

Debt structure is short-dated relative to the long tail: a meaningful slice of borrowings matures within the next twelve months alongside commercial paper, so refinancing is recurring even though the maturity ladder beyond year five is long and cash balances are ample.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow covers debt by a wide margin and improved sharply year over year, well above the sector median, indicating debt service is comfortably funded from internal cash generation rather than refinancing.

Operating cash flow exceeds dividends plus buybacks, so distributions are funded internally and do not erode the debt-service buffer; interest coverage cannot be assessed because interest expense is not disclosed in the tagged data, a material gap for a leveraged peer comparison.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is Minimal, driven by leverage and cash-flow coverage both in the lowest tier; the balance sheet carries modest net debt after cash and investments, and the Altman zone is Safe, supporting a strong investment-grade posture.

Our forward view is stable: margins and cash conversion should hold, but rising component costs, tariff exposure and heavy buyback absorption of free cash flow are the watch items; liquidity is adequate though the current ratio trails the sector median.

credit_strengths.text: 經營利潤率按年擴張，並顯著高於行業中位數，反映硬件定價能力及日益增長的服務業務組合；此盈利質素支撐現金創造，即使管理層討論與分析已指出供應驅動的成本壓力。
總槓桿較上年下降，並仍遠低於行業中位數，而以現金及投資計算的淨槓桿則深處最低風險區間，距下一門檻尚有充裕緩衝。

key_risks.text: 風險因素凸顯對大型離岸供應鏈及非美國銷售的依賴，不利宏觀環境、關稅及貿易爭端可打擊需求、零部件成本及應收賬款；管理層討論與分析確認記憶體及儲存成本通脹預計將加劇。
債務結構相對於長尾而言屬短期限：相當一部分借款連同商業票據將於未來十二個月內到期，故再融資屬經常性，儘管五年以後的到期階梯較長且現金結餘充裕。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流以較大差距覆蓋債務，並按年大幅改善，遠高於行業中位數，顯示償債能力由內部現金創造從容支持，而非依賴再融資。
經營現金流超過股息加回購，故分派由內部資金支持，不會侵蝕償債緩衝；利息覆蓋率無法評估，因標籤數據未披露利息支出，此乃與槓桿同業比較的重大缺口。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為極低，由槓桿及現金流覆蓋均處最低級別所驅動；資產負債表在計入現金及投資後淨債務溫和，而 Altman 區域為安全，支撐強勁的投資級態勢。
我們的前瞻觀點為穩定：利潤率及現金轉換應可維持，但零部件成本上升、關稅敞口及大量回購吸收自由現金流為需關注事項；流動性充足，儘管流動比率落後於行業中位數。
